 Palantir and AMD Just Reported Earnings. History Says This Will Happen to Both Stocks Next.

 PLTR +3.77% 
 NVDA +3.91%

 Learn more Chipmaker AMD (NASDAQ: AMD) and data analytics giant Palantir (NASDAQ: PLTR) each reported their third-quarter earnings results earlier this week. In the aftermath of those reports, Palantir's stock declined slightly while AMD's rose. While both companies' numbers showed that their businesses are growing rapidly, I think investors need to focus on something else: the valuations of their stocks. 
 These companies are trading at sky-high valuation levels, and history is not on their side. 
 Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue » 
 Image source: Getty Images. AMD and Palantir have a ton of future growth baked into their stocks 
 Finding businesses that are doing well to invest in is just one part of the equation for investors. Their stocks also have to be purchasable at a reasonable price. How best to determine what a reasonable price would be for any given stock is a widely debated topic, as there are a host of factors that can affect that calculation, from the industry it operates in to its track record to overall sector sentiment. However, there are some broadly acceptable valuation ranges that most stocks tend to trade within. 
 Both AMD and Palantir are mature businesses, and their profit margins are not expected to expand rapidly over the next few years, so the price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio is a great metric to use to gauge their valuations. However, both of them are also growing fast. During Q3, Palantir's growth rate rose to 96%. AMD's top line rose at a slower 45% pace, but that's still quite impressive. In light of those growth rates, I don't think the trailing P/E ratio is the best valuation measure here, as it looks at where companies have been, not where they're going. 
 Instead, I think valuing these companies relative to their projected earnings makes far more sense. With 2026 almost over, using 2027 estimates is a good idea. And by that measure, it's easy to see how expensive Palantir and AMD are. 
 AMD PE Ratio (Forward 1y) data by YCharts. 
 Palantir clearly takes the cake for being very pricey, as 71 times forward earnings is way more than most stocks trade for. Its forward P/E ratio is more than double AMD's -- a huge red flag. And while the chipmaker looks relatively more reasonable at 30 times next year's earnings, it's worth noting that AMD's top competitor, Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA), trades for just 13 times forward earnings and is posting better results. 
 Story Continues While stocks can temporarily become expensive, over the long term, they tend to revert to normal valuation levels. That could be a problem for both Palantir and AMD. While I'm not saying that a crash is imminent for either or both of them, their high valuations could indicate that a period of stock price underperformance is coming as their valuations normalize. 
 As a result, I think investors should steer clear of these two, as there are far better options available.
